prediction.likelyOutcome: Montgomery Park is more likely than not to prevail on its core position that NCO's early termination was invalid and that rent obligations continued past May 2011, given NCO's admitted vacatur over the landlord's express notice of non-compliance — but this is a contested bench trial, not a conceded or defaulted liability picture. On the documented record, Montgomery Park should recover at least the $313,662.76 arrearage identified in its 2011 default letter plus default-rate interest, with attorney's fees a likely but currently unquantifiable additional recovery under the lease's fee-shifting clause; NCO's overcharge, unjust enrichment, and fraud counterclaims are unlikely to produce an offsetting recovery of any magnitude given the absence of any stated overcharge figure and the general difficulty of proving fraud in this posture.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court entered judgment for Montgomery Park on its past-due-rent counterclaim of $9,854,566.95 plus postjudgment interest (upheld in earlier Fourth Circuit appeals at 842 F.3d 816, 918 F.3d 388 and 40 F.4th 123). The court then awarded $2,074,379.88 in attorneys' fees and nontaxable expenses, $115,942.10 taxable costs and $1,576,036.07 default interest ($3,766,358.05 total). In this fifth appeal the Fourth Circuit affirmed the fee/cost award (including expert fees) but vacated the default-interest component, holding interest runs only from the August 24, 2022 demand, and remanded for recalculation; the underlying rent judgment was not disturbed.
